subject.title: [Bug] Silent fail-open when Tailscale interface binding fails on gateway start

question: When explicit `gateway.bind: "tailnet"` cannot obtain a bindable Tailscale IPv4, should startup remain locally available with a prominent degraded-state warning, or fail closed with a non-zero exit?
rationale: Both choices are defensible: loopback fallback preserves local recovery and does not widen exposure, while fatal startup more strictly enforces explicit network intent; repository policy treats fallback removal and startup failure as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Warn and degrade locally
options.body: Keep the loopback-only fallback, surface a clear startup/status warning, and add contract tests and aligned docs.

options.title: Fail explicit tailnet closed
options.body: Exit non-zero whenever no bindable Tailnet IPv4 is available, accepting the resulting startup and upgrade availability impact.

options.title: Keep current silent fallback
options.body: Retain current runtime behavior without new diagnostics, leaving remote failure as the main signal.

recommendation.title: Warn and degrade locally
recommendation.body: Keep the loopback-only fallback, surface a clear startup/status warning, and add contract tests and aligned docs.

likelyOwner.reason: This account introduced explicit tailnet binding and has the strongest continuing history across gateway/Tailscale behavior and hardening.
